newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France to decide on Thomson in "coming days".
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France to decide on Thomson in "coming days".

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Tuesday the state would decide "in the coming days" on the privatisation of electronics group Thomson, adding reports a decision had been taken were "beyond the truth".
A decision on the future of the large state company had been expected at the start of the week and at the latest after Wednesday's government cabinet meeting.

"The government will take a decision on the privatisation of Thomson in the coming days. Our preference will be communicated to the privatisation commission," Arthuis told parliament during question time.

Asked to comment on speculation the government had already decided, after consultation with President Jacques Chirac, to sell the company to Alcatel-Alsthom, Arthuis said that such a scenario "was beyond the truth".

Alcatel and Lagardere Groupe are both in the race to buy Thomson SA, which has full ownership of Thomson Multimedia -- one of the world's leading television makers -- as well as a 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF which is among the top five world defence electronics companies.
Arthuis did not indicate whether the state would make a capital injection to Thomson prior to privatisation but said a lack of state action was behind Thomson's problems.
"One of the reasons that Thomson is in difficulties is because the state has always refused to make a capital injection," he said.

Both bidders have unveiled the main lines of their business plan for Thomson but neither has detailed the financial elements of their bids. French newspapers speculate the state may have to pump billions of francs into Thomson prior to the transfer.
Thomson SA is 76 percent owned by the state while 20 percent is held by telecommunications operator France Telecom.

Thomson SA made a 1995 loss of 1.379 billion francs ($266 million) and has debts of some 25 billion francs, of which 14 billion are at the multimedia arm which made a 1995 loss of 1.09 billion francs.
Thomson-CSF returned to the black in 1995 with a profit of 1.01 billion francs. Thomson-CSF has a 20 percent stake in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV.
Lagardere Groupe, led by its founder Jean-Luc Lagardere, is a conglomerate with interests spanning from the media business to its Matra defence business.
Lagardere plans to control Thomson-CSF while British Aerospace Plc, GEC Plc and perhaps Daimler-Benz Aerospace GmbH (DASA) could take minority stakes.
Lagardere has lined up South Korea's Daewoo to run Thomson Multimedia. Daewoo's chairman said he saw synergies in components and he has promised to create jobs in France.
Alcatel-Alsthom unveiled its Thomson plans on September 18.
Alcatel wants to hoist Thomson-CSF to the number two spot of the world defence industry, behind Lockheed Martin but ahead of GM Hughes Electronics Corp.
For that, it plans a "wide-scale partnership with another major industrial player" in Britain, Germany or both.
